prompts.text: Name a professional sports league with at least 10 teams

items.quip: Ten franchises played one season, 1961–62, then it folded.
items.title: National Bowling League
items.extract: The National Bowling League (NBL) is a defunct professional bowling league in the United States that existed from February 24, 1960 to July 9, 1962. The league was formed as an attempt to ride the popularity of bowling television shows, and also to challenge the Professional Bowlers Association (PBA).

items.quip: Its 1884 champion St Louis Maroons finished 94–19.
items.title: Union Association
items.extract: The Union Association was an American professional baseball league which competed with Major League Baseball, lasting for just the 1884 season. St. Louis won the pennant and joined the National League the following season.

prompts.text: Name a living animal that weighs over a metric ton (1,000 kg)

items.quip: Fewer than a hundred survive, all in the Gulf of Mexico.
items.title: Rice's whale
items.extract: Rice's whale, also known as the Gulf of Mexico whale, is a species of baleen whale endemic to the northern Gulf of Mexico. Initially identified as a subpopulation of the Bryde's whale, genetic and skeletal studies found it to be a distinct species in 2021. In outward appearance, it is virtually identical to the Bryde's whale. Its body is streamlined and sleek, with a uniformly dark charcoal gray dorsal and pale to pinkish underside. A diagnostic feature often used by field scientists to distinguish Rice's whales from whales other than the Bryde's whale is the three prominent ridges that line the top of its head. The species can be distinguished from the Bryde's whale by the shape of the nasal bones, which have wider gaps due to a unique wrapping by the frontal bones, its unique vocal repertoire, and genetic differences.

items.quip: Poland bred this wisent-cattle hybrid as a hardier cow.
items.title: Żubroń
items.extract: Żubroń is a hybrid of a domestic cattle and a wisent. The wisent is the European bison; hence, the żubroń is analogous to the American cattalo. The name żubroń was officially chosen from hundreds of proposals sent to the Polish weekly magazine Przekrój during a contest organised in 1969.

prompts.text: Name a city south of the equator whose metropolitan area has over 1 million people (main cities only)

items.quip: Diamonds built a city bigger than you probably imagined.
items.title: Mbuji-Mayi
items.description: Provincial capital and city in Kasai-Oriental, Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.extract: Mbuji-Mayi is a city and the capital of Kasai-Oriental Province in the south-central Democratic Republic of Congo. It is thought to be the second largest city in the country, after the capital Kinshasa and ahead of Lubumbashi, Kisangani and Kananga, though its exact population is not known. Estimates range from a 2010 CIA World Factbook estimated population of 1,480,000 to as many as 3,500,000 estimated by the United Nations in 2008.

prompts.text: Name an app or service meant for editing photos

items.quip: Adobe bought its publisher Aldus in 1994 and shelved it.
items.title: Aldus PhotoStyler
items.extract: Aldus PhotoStyler was a graphics software program developed by the Taiwanese company Ulead. Released in June 1991 as the first 24 bit image editor for Windows, it was bought the same year by the Aldus Prepress group. Its main competition was Adobe Photoshop. Version 2.0 introduced a new user interface and improved color calibration. PhotoStyler SE - lacking some features of the version 2.0 - was bundled with scanners like HP ScanJet. The product disappeared from the Adobe product line after Adobe acquired Aldus in 1994.
